subject: How to specify an OU anisotropic movement model

messages.author: 0cb1ab1dff2bfeb6
messages.subject: How to specify an OU anisotropic movement model
parts:
Hello,

I have some gila monster home range data, and I've determined that the location data of one individual best fits an OU anisotropic model according to its AIC score. My issue is that I'm not certain how to specify an OU anisotropic movement model. I've read in the help section for ctmm.select that the OU model is indicated by length(tau)==1. I'm not quite sure where to add that into my code, and so far my attempts are ending with an error message (see code below).  If I understand the process correctly (which I'm not sure that I do) the first step is to specify the CTMM object, then feed that into the ctmm.select function to create the movement model. Have I put length(tau)==1 in the right place? Does the value of tau itself need manipulating? What else should I do to specify the OU anisotropic movement model? Apologies for any unnecessary code below, I wasn't sure what to leave out from the help pane example. Thank you for any help,

Jason


CTMM<-ctmm(tau=NULL, length(tau)==1,omega=FALSE, isotropic=FALSE, range=TRUE, circle=FALSE, error=FALSE, axes=c("x","y"))
M.OUA <- ctmm.select(Gila.5,CTMM,verbose=FALSE, level=1,IC="AICc",MSPE="position", trace=FALSE, cores=1) 

Error in ctmm.iterate(data, CTMM, verbose = verbose, level = level, IC = IC, : trying to get slot "par" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with no slots

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] How to specify an OU anisotropic movement model
parts:
Hi Jason,

If you run:

guess <- ctmm.guess(l, interactive=FALSE)
fit <- ctmm.select(l, guess)

where l is the telemetry object, then fit will automatically be the best-fit model. You don’t need to specify anything in this case, just make sure the model fits the variogram OK after it is fit.

Jesse
